answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after a long, verifiable history of useful work, like a bridge that charges its toll in time rather than tokens. An attacker faces an ocean of cost to flood the network with fakes, since every copy must pay the same deposit and wait out the same aging period. Honest agents get their deposit back at dawn of each settlement cycle if their work checks out, while detected fakes forfeit theirs, so spinning up thousands of identities costs thousands of deposits and earns nothing.
